subject: Mutual Action Plan: Performance runbook, access, and load windows
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@cloudwave.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@cloudwave.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Benchmarking + MAP kickoff

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our CTO wants a short mutual action plan that covers the performance validation we discussed (latency, throughput, TTFT, and concurrency), plus logistics for accessing our pre-prod cluster so your team can run the load windows.

Can you share a draft MAP and a proposed schedule for a 48-hour profiling window? We have two SREs (cc'd) who can provision test accounts; ideally we'd run tests the week of Jan 25.

Attached: initial-requirements.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Aisha Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, Cloudwave
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@cloudwave.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:45:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Benchmarking + MAP kickoff

Hi Aisha —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've attached a one-page MAP and a runbook draft that outlines objectives, success criteria, and the proposed test matrix:
- Latency P95/P99 at 4 sequence profiles
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) at target concurrency levels (8, 32, 128)
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) SLOs for cold vs warm cache
- KV cache priming steps and rollback plan

Suggested load windows (pick one):
1) Jan 25 02:00–04:00 UTC (low-traffic overnight) — preferred
2) Jan 26 14:00–16:00 UTC

Next steps for Cloudwave SREs: provide a test service account + IAM role with read-only access to the test bucket, and two short-lived API keys. Aditya will send the exact format we need for key rotation and ingestion. Karthik will own the test harness and will share the runner config.

Attachments: cloudwave-map-v1.pdf (MAP), access-instructions.txt (stub)

If those windows work, we'll book the slot and run a dry run (smoke) 24 hours beforehand.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: DevOps Team <sre@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Access details we need for the Jan 25 run (short list)

Hi Cloudwave SREs —

Following Hannah's MAP, quick list of what we'll need to run the profiling window cleanly:
- Two short-lived API keys (one for load generator, one for verification)
- A test service account with role 'test-runner' scoped to the pre-prod inference endpoint
- Endpoint URL + TLS cert thumbprint (if mutual TLS required)
- Test dataset location (S3/GCS path) and a read-only token
- Preferred bastion host details (if access via jump host)

Example key format we accept is in access-instructions.txt (attached). We can consume keys with a 24-hour TTL; if you prefer time-boxed SSH, tell us window start/end times and we'll coordinate.

Quote from Hannah's MAP below for convenience:
> Objectives: validate P95/P99 latency across 4 sequence profiles, verify TTFT under cold/warm cache, measure sustained tokens/sec at target concurrency and verify graceful degradation above capacity.

Thanks — if someone can confirm provisioning timeline (and which window you prefer), we'll lock the calendar.

—Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@cloudwave.com>, Samir Patel <samir@cloudwave.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jan 2026 20:10:05 -0800
Subject: Performance run results — Jan 25 profiling window (summary)

Hi all —

We completed the 48-hour profiling window on Jan 25 (slot 1). Attached is the raw CSV (perf-results-20260125.csv) and a short summary below. Note: tests were run against the pre-prod endpoint using the test-runner keys provided by Cloudwave; KV cache was primed for warm runs.

Summary (highlight):
- Concurrency sweep: 8 / 32 / 128 workers
- Sustained tokens/sec (mean): 8 workers = 1,350 t/s; 32 workers = 5,200 t/s; 128 workers = 18,900 t/s
- Latency P95 / P99 (cold cache): 8w = 210ms / 415ms; 32w = 330ms / 720ms; 128w = 1,100ms / 2,300ms
- Latency P95 / P99 (warm cache): 8w = 135ms / 220ms; 32w = 220ms / 340ms; 128w = 680ms / 1,050ms
- TTFT (median): cold = 120ms; warm = 40ms
- Observations: KV cache priming reduced P99 by ~60% for medium-length sequences. Above 128 workers we observed queuing and elevated tail latency; we recommend a soft limit of 100 concurrent in this configuration or enabling batch-adaptive scaling.

Action items:
- We will upload a short runbook change proposing autoscaling threshold adjustments (will attach in follow-up).
- Marissa, can you schedule a 30-min readout with procurement to align on close timeline given these perf numbers?

Attachments: perf-results-20260125.csv (CSV)

-Karthik Iyer
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@cloudwave.com>, Samir Patel <samir@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Feb 2026 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: MAP signoff & next steps toward close (proposed timeline)

Hi Aisha / Samir —

Thanks for running the window with us and to your SREs for the quick provisioning. The data Karthik shared shows we meet your P95 targets at expected concurrency and identifies the safe concurrency operating point. Per the MAP, the remaining items to close:
1) Finalize order form & signature (we'll send DocuSign link once you confirm procurement owner).
2) Agree on scheduled autoscaling thresholds (we'll provide recommended values in a short change doc).
3) Production roll plan (can be a phased rollout; Redwood will provide playbooks and rollback).

Proposed close timeline:
- Feb 4: Procurement confirms PO amount & sig authority
- Feb 9: DocuSign executed (target)
- Feb 16: Kickoff for production onboarding (technical onboarding & knowledge transfer)

Related links: MAP + raw results folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CloudwaveMAP), HubSpot deal CW-1127 (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345).

Marissa — please coordinate procurement outreach; happy to join the call.

If you want us to tighten tail latency further, we can propose a quantization + batching experiment as an optional add-on and include projected cost impact.

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: cloudwave-map-v1.pdf, access-instructions.txt, perf-results-20260125.csv
